title: BeforeShare closed enumerations
description: Every enumeration here is CLOSED. A consumer that encounters a value it does not know must fail visibly (§20.3) rather than skip the item or degrade it to a default.

status.description: Aggregate outcome of one inspection run. The decision rules that produce this value are owned by issue #18 and are NOT defined by this schema.

severity.description: How much unintended disclosure this finding represents if the file is shared as-is. Severity describes the finding, never the confidence in it - that is `certainty`.

certainty.description: deterministic: produced by a format parser or an explicit rule over structured data. probabilistic: produced by OCR, a model, or a heuristic over free text. Carried per finding, not per category: the same category can arrive by either path (§7.3).

remediationAction.description: The eight actions required by §9.1. PDF metadata removal and image metadata removal are kept as SEPARATE values even though both write metadata: they touch different parsers, carry different side effects (an image rewrite can alter orientation; a PDF rewrite can invalidate a signature), and a capability declaration must be able to say that one format supports it and the other does not. No action may be added here without a corresponding verification path (§10.1); an action nothing can verify must not be offered.

sideEffect.description: The six warning classes required by §9.2. alters_visual_rendering covers colour, font rendering, image quality, page dimensions and file size.

unsupportedReason.description: Required whenever remediation.supported is false. 'Why can this not be fixed' is user-facing information, not an internal detail.

limitationCode.description: A limitation narrows what a clean result is allowed to mean. Every limitation must name the detectors it affects, so that `no_findings` can never be produced while a limitation silently suppressed a check. `ocr_not_available` is this build having no OCR at all, which the two codes beside it do not say: they are answers from an OCR that ran and found the picture too small or the language unsupported.
